title: Caroline Herschel's birth chart
metaDescription: Caroline Herschel's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.8° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 13.1° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 25.8° Pisces, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mars. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 2.2° Pisces, Venus at 16.8° Aries, Mars at 13.3° Taurus. Mercury in a water sign reads as thought steeped in tone and memory; Venus in a fire sign reads as attraction declared rather than implied; Mars in an earth sign reads as effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.1° wide. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, the Sun trine Neptune at 0.8°, and Mercury square Pluto at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. The Moon in Cancer at 13.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Pisces at 2.2° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Aries at 16.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Taurus at 13.3° is in detriment. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 water, 4 fire, 1 earth, 1 air by element and 4 mutable, 4 cardinal, 2 fixed by mode. Venus, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.6° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 13.1°.
